items.title: A non-exported trait impl in a module with an EXPLICIT export surface, reached from a library's generic body through a bound, fails with `'find' is provided by an impl in module X, and module lib does not admit it ... Widen lib's own import of X` - advice a library cannot follow; the fix is `export impl` on the caller's impl, which the message never names
items.kind: diagnostic (B318 import surface; generic bodies over user impls)
items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-11-06 (the integrator's find in the reactive lens lab, A185)
items.discussion: minimal repro on 0.54.0: lib.vl declares `export trait Look<K,V> { fun find(self, key: K): Option<V>; }` and `export fun look_up<S: Look<K,V>, K, V>(held: S, key: K): Option<V> { held.find(key) }`; main.vl has `impl Tabs with Look<i32,i32>` (NOT exported), ANY `export fun` (even `export fun probe(w: i32): i32 { w }`), and calls `look_up(Tabs{..}, 7)`. Fails as quoted. Remove the `export fun` (the module falls back to `export *;`) or write `export impl` and it passes. The lens lab met it with a `Lookup` impl beside an exported helper; kolt is mostly `export *;` (70 of 92 files) so it rarely shows there
items.body: Rec: (1) when the unadmitted impl lives in the module that INSTANTIATED the generic (or in any module with an explicit surface) say `mark it `export impl Tabs with Look<i32, i32>`` instead of telling the library to widen its import; (2) owner Q: should an impl reached only through a BOUND need the export at all? The caller passed the value, so the caller chose the impl; admitting bound-dispatched impls regardless of the surface would spare every shape-trait author the rule. Pin: the repro above as an `assert_fails` with the new wording, and its `export impl` twin compiling. Sizing S for (1); (2) is a B318 ruling.
